question: A vertical pole TF has its base F on the ground. From a point A, 25 meters from F, the angle of elevation of T is x°. From another point B, 75 meters from F (and in the same line as A), the angle of elevation of T is y°. If the height of the pole is 25√3 meters, what is the value of x° + y°?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the tangent ratio for both points A and B directly:

tan(x) = Height ÷ Distance A = 25√3 ÷ 25 = √3 ⇒ x = 60°

tan(y) = Height ÷ Distance B = 25√3 ÷ 75 = 1/√3 ⇒ y = 30°

Sum of angles = x + y = 60° + 30° = 90°.

**∴ The correct answer is 90°.**
